title: Choose a text that needs the skill
statement: Choose each practice text after the skill it is for, so that the skill is the only way through it, never a text the learner already knows or can guess.
detail: A Grade 3 reading course's teaching-move note, drawn from IES and What Works Clearinghouse practice-guide videos, says to pick the passage after the target strategy and so that the strategy is the only way through, since on a text whose ending the child already knows a prediction lesson measures familiarity, not the skill (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/g3-reading-red-team/references/teaching-moves/strategy-text-fit.md`). One of its checks gives the passage to a fresh model with the strategy stripped out: if it still answers the item, the text does not make the strategy necessary.

evidence.quote: Pick the passage *after* you pick the target strategy, and pick it so the strategy is the only way through.
we really want to select a text for teaching that strategy where using that strategy is going to really help you understand the text
the item measures familiarity, not the skill
if it answers the target item correctly without applying the strategy, the text does not make the strategy necessary.

citations.ref: IES practice-guide video, Improving Reading Comprehension in Kindergarten Through 3rd Grade, part 4
